svg.title: glia-nav: how a request moves through the system
svg.desc: Web path, agent path, and daily ingest meet at one Aurora database reached over the RDS Data API. Opened in a browser, each box has a note on what it does and why, and links to the service documentation.

g.title: What happens when a visitor searches or asks a question.
How a chat message becomes a cited answer.
How the database fills and stays current.
One database, reached only over HTTPS. No network route in.
Everything that watches, alarms on, or ships the stacks above.
No route in or out. A NAT gateway would cost about $32/month for internet access nothing here needs. An S3 gateway endpoint (free) covers bucket access.
Search goes through Amplify's same-origin rewrite.
Chat calls App Runner's URL under its 120 s limit; Amplify's proxy would cut it at 30 s. CORS allows this one origin.
Keyword (tsvector) and vector (pgvector) search, fused by reciprocal rank fusion.
One runtime session per conversation, id public-<uuid>.
search_trials_and_papers, with the runtime role's signature.
The Gateway's outbound auth carries a Cognito client-credentials token; the API accepts /search without checking it.
Trials by LastUpdatePostDate, papers by entry and modification date, from one day before the last watermark.
Every write is an upsert, so a repeated run is safe.
The Data API resolves the master password from its Secrets Manager ARN using the caller's IAM identity.
AgentCore and App Runner logs and metrics land here.
Evaluations read agent spans from the aws/spans log group.
Both alarms publish to the alerts topic.
Budget notifications go to the same topic.
Actions assumes the deploy role over OIDC; no stored keys.
cdk deploy for all six stacks, then the Amplify upload.
CDK pushes the three container images as assets.
Input. A static Next.js page with two tabs: Search and Ask the navigator. Nothing is stored about the visitor.

a.title: Serves the static site from a CDN and rewrites /api/* to App Runner on the same origin, so search needs no CORS. Chat skips the rewrite because it cuts requests off at 30 s.

Runs the API container with TLS, health checks, and autoscaling, and no load balancer to operate. Pinned to one 0.25 vCPU instance: uncapped scale-out is the biggest budget risk. /search fuses keyword and vector results; /chat invokes the agent and waits out a paused cluster first.
Titan Text Embeddings V2, 512 dimensions. /search embeds the query so the vector half of the search can find matches that share meaning but not words.
Anonymises names, emails, phones, addresses, and ages; blocks SSNs and card numbers. Applied by the service, so it cannot be prompted away. Runs in sync mode so streamed chunks are masked.

Model inference through a us. inference profile. IAM pins invocation to six model IDs. The agent runs on the large tier; extraction and routing use Haiku. Cache points sit after the system prompt and tool definitions.

Serverless hosting for the agent with session isolation and OTEL tracing built in. One chat is one session, so follow-ups work without the API storing history. The agent has no database credentials: data comes through the Gateway.
Turns the backend's OpenAPI document into MCP tools (search_trials_and_papers). Inbound auth is IAM (SigV4 from the runtime role), so tool access is an IAM decision, not a shared token.

The Gateway fetches a scoped access token for the glia-nav-gateway client from AgentCore Identity's token vault and sends it to the backend. Cognito also holds the user pool for /me. /search and /chat take no token.
One cron schedule invokes the ingest Lambda once a day. No retries: every write is an upsert, so the next run catches up.
Input. CT.gov v2 JSON and PubMed efetch XML. Both are on the public internet, which is why the Lambda runs outside the VPC. Retries five times on 500s, 429s, and truncated bodies.

Pulls the day's changes from both sources, embeds new or changed text, reads eligibility into structured fields, and upserts through the Data API. Its role can reach this cluster, the raw/ prefix, Titan, and Haiku, and nothing else.

Titan embeds each chunk (hash-checked, so unchanged text is never re-embedded). Haiku 4.5 reads each trial's criteria into IDH, MGMT, recurrence, bevacizumab, and KPS fields through a forced tool call; code checks its answers against quotes from the criteria.
The Data API resolves the password from its ARN using the caller's IAM identity. The value never reaches a container, .env, or a developer's shell.
The only way in. App code, Alembic migrations, and local scripts all query over HTTPS with IAM, so the cluster needs no NAT, no VPC connector, no bastion.

One engine for trial and paper records and their embeddings, so there is no second datastore. 0 to 1 ACU, auto-pauses after 5 minutes; idle cost is storage only. The first call after a pause returns 503 resuming.
Keeps each source's raw payload under raw/ctgov/ and raw/pubmed/ so records can be re-parsed without calling the sources again. Versioned, SSE-S3, public access blocked, Infrequent Access at 30 days.
JSON logs from both containers. Metric filters pull token counts into the glia-nav namespace. Alarms on any runtime error and on 200,000 tokens a day. Every log group is set to 30 day retention.
Indexes 100 percent of agent spans into the aws/spans log group. Without it the spans stay in X-Ray and there is nothing to evaluate.
Response relevance and tool selection accuracy on production traces. The local golden set in evals/ is the pre-deploy gate; this is the post-deploy one.
One topic carries both CloudWatch alarms and the budget notifications.
Tracks gross usage, not net, because promotional credits would hold net spend at $0.00 and the thresholds could never fire.
ci.yml on pull requests, deploy.yml on merge to main. Every merge runs the tests and the golden-set eval before deploying.
GitHub Actions assumes a role through the OIDC provider with a 1 hour session cap. No access keys exist in the repo or the account.
One CDK app in Python, one stack per concern: Ops, Data, Backend, Agent, Frontend, Ingest. An app-level aspect tags every resource project=glia-nav, env=dev, managed-by=cdk.
Where CDK's Docker assets land. App Runner (amd64), AgentCore (arm64), and Lambda (arm64) all pull from it.
AgentStack publishes the runtime ARN and FrontendStack the site origin as parameters, because CloudFormation rejects the import cycle a direct reference would create.
